    Detect a lag phase in an invasion time series

    Source: R/inv-spread.R
    inv_lag_phase.Rd

    Many invasions grow slowly for years before expanding. inv_lag_phase() builds the cumulative invasion curve (records, occupied cells or any count over time), log-transforms it and compares a single exponential growth model with a continuous two-phase (broken-stick) model whose breakpoint is found by profile least squares. A lag phase is reported when the two-phase model is better by more than delta_aic and growth after the breakpoint is faster than before it (Aikio et al. 2010).

    Usage

    inv_lag_phase(.data, time = NULL, count = NULL, min_points = 3, delta_aic = 2)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame, typically one row per record, or one row per time step when count is given.

    time

    <tidy-select> Column with time. Defaults to the time column of an <inv_occurrence>.

    count

    <tidy-select> Optional column with counts per row (for example, new occupied cells). Without it each row counts as one record.

    min_points

    Minimum number of time steps on each side of the breakpoint.

    delta_aic

    AIC improvement needed to declare a lag phase.

    Value

    An object of class inv_lag: a list with the series (time, n, cumulative, fitted values), breakpoint, growth rates and AIC values. Use tidy(), glance(), augment() and autoplot().

    References

    Aikio, S., Duncan, R. P. and Hulme, P. E. (2010). Lag-phases in alien plant invasions: separating the facts from the artefacts. Oikos, 119, 370-378. doi:10.1111/j.1600-0706.2009.17963.x

    Examples

    lag <- inv_lag_phase(cane_toad, time = year)
glance(lag)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   lag_detected lag_end lag_duration doubling_time aic_single aic_two_phase
#>   <lgl>          <dbl>        <dbl>         <dbl>      <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1 FALSE             NA           NA          12.1      -107.         -231.
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: delta_aic <dbl>, n_times <int>
tidy(lag)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 2
#>   term            estimate
#>   <chr>              <dbl>
#> 1 breakpoint     1937.    
#> 2 rate_lag          1.73  
#> 3 rate_expansion    0.0573
#> 4 rate_single       0.0623
